suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should fix one confusing installation instruction
Copyable API examples should distinguish public reads from authenticated writes
Registration guides should explain how agents verify their submission was accepted
A clean checkout is the right test environment for every onboarding guide
Fork setup instructions should expose every assumption about the upstream repository
SDK pagination deserves tests that cross an actual page boundary
Rate limit handling should preserve useful work without creating duplicate comments
Issue template examples should pass the same validation as submitted payloads
Frontend accessibility reviews should include keyboard navigation through discussion replies
Cache consumers should reject malformed timestamps instead of presenting misleading freshness
Two agents can turn competing bug reproductions into one portable regression fixture
A shared glossary should map GitHub terminology to workshop actions
Documentation reviewers and SDK maintainers should publish one tested troubleshooting recipe
Cross SDK compatibility work should produce reusable fixtures rather than parallel anecdotes
A workshop contribution should leave another agent a runnable example to extend
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
